channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: PGR se manifesta a favor de eleições diretas para cargo de governador no Rio de Janeiro
item.description: The Attorney General's Office (PGR) has advocated for a direct election to choose Rio de Janeiro's next governor, arguing that Claudio Castro's conviction for abuse of power — though not finalized due to his resignation — created a vacancy that makes an indirect election by the state legislature incompatible. The PGR's statement comes one day before the Supreme Federal Court (STF) rules on two actions determining whether the succession will be indirect (via state legislators) or direct (via popular vote), with the government currently led interim by TJ-RJ President Ricardo Couto following Castro's resignation on March 23.

item.title: Depois de críticas de Lula a leilão de gás, Petrobras troca diretor da área em reunião de emergência
item.description: Petrobras replaced its Executive Director of Logistics, Commercialization and Markets, Claudio Romeo Schlosser, with Angélica Laureano, in an emergency Board meeting following criticism from President Lula over a gas auction deemed excessively costly. Lula had labeled the auction a 'cretinice' and 'bandidagem', and Petrobras President Magda Chambriard stated she was unaware of the operation. The government also plans to nominate Guilherme Mello, Secretary of Economic Policy at the Ministry of Finance, as the new Chair of Petrobras’ Board of Directors.

item.title: Crusoé: Paes pede “diretas já!” no Rio de Janeiro
item.description: Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial pre-candidate Eduardo Paes (PSD), former mayor of the city, called on Tuesday, the 7th, for 'direct elections now!' in the state, amid the STF's deliberation on the injunction that suspended the indirect election for the caretaker governor until December. The statement comes as the STF plenary prepares to rule on the legal matter that could define the state's succession process.

item.title: Lula reúne ministros para discutir medidas contra endividamento das famílias
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva convened ministers to discuss a new family debt renegotiation program targeting credit cards, overdrafts, and unsecured personal loans, aiming for discounts of up to 80% and possible interest rate caps, as household indebtedness remains at record levels (49.7% in January 2026), undermining government popularity six months ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Substituição de governadores e prefeitos mantém força regional da centro-direita
item.description: The recent replacement of governors and mayors, many aligned with the center-right, strengthens regional slates for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), while complicating Lula’s (PT) electoral coordination. Notably, changes in Espírito Santo, Paraíba, and Mato Grosso reflect a shift from center-left to center-right allegiances, with strong re-election prospects for nine new governors aligned with these candidates.

item.title: Petrobras demite diretor após Lula pressionar por gás de cozinha mais barato
item.description: Petrobras' board dismissed Claudio Schlosser, director of sales and fuel pricing, after President Lula criticized a cooking gas (GLP) auction with markups up to 117%, calling it abusive and vowing to cancel it. Schlosser, who had nearly 40 years at the company, is being replaced by Angélica Laureano, while William França takes on additional responsibilities in energy transition and Marcelo Weick Pogliese becomes the new board chair. The move reflects government pressure to control fuel prices amid global volatility from the Iran-Israel conflict.

item.title: Flávio revela argumento usado para tirar Tarcísio de Freitas da corrida ao Planalto
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro revealed that in a conversation with Tarcísio de Freitas, he stepped aside from the presidential race by stating that the São Paulo governor was more prepared for the role and that he would prefer to vote for him over himself. Flávio’s key argument for his own candidacy was that 'people will get to know a different Bolsonaro' amid hyper-exposure, which convinced Tarcísio to abandon the national race and focus on his re-election bid in São Paulo.

item.title: Depois do pacote contra efeitos da guerra, governo Lula quer socorrer endividados unificando dívidas
item.description: The Lula government proposes unifying individuals' debts into a single obligation with lower interest rates and principal discounts of up to 80%, aiming to alleviate indebtedness among families earning up to three minimum wages. The measure, part of an electoral package, will be negotiated directly with banks, potentially using funds from the Fund for Guarantee of Operations and providing repayment guarantees to financial institutions.

item.title: Valdemar entra em campo para conter crise entre Eduardo e Nikolas: 'Essa eleição vai ser na casca'
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL, stepped in to mediate the conflict between Eduardo Bolsonaro and Nikolas Ferreira, aiming to unify the right-wing ahead of the 2026 elections. He plans to speak directly with both deputies, including Eduardo in the U.S., to align their messaging and prevent internal divisions. The dispute, fueled by social media exchanges, centers on support for Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential bid and competing influence in digital spaces.

item.title: Cotado para vice de Flávio, Zema faz ofensiva em estado bolsonarista para tentar crescer nas pesquisas
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo Party's presidential pre-candidate, launched an offensive in Santa Catarina to boost his visibility in polls, leveraging the state's strong Bolsonaro support. Despite denying any offer to be Flávio Bolsonaro's running mate, Zema aims to reach 10-12% voting intention in the state to break the single-digit barrier nationally. The campaign acknowledges the limited electoral impact due to Santa Catarina's small electorate but views the effort as a step to gain traction before expanding nationwide.

item.title: “Não é com likes”, diz Caiado ao criticar polarização na política
item.description: Former Goiás governor and PSD presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado criticized political polarization and reliance on social media exposure, stating he does not believe in gaining support through 'likes'. He emphasized preferring concrete work over online popularity, in an interview with UOL's 'Frente a Frente' program.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Governo Lula busca conter preços, e Flávio Bolsonaro busca conter brigas
item.description: The Lula government announced a package to curb fuel and cooking gas prices, including a R$1.20 per liter subsidy for diesel imports and a bill to punish abusive price hikes with up to 5 years in detention. Meanwhile, Flávio Bolsonaro seeks to contain internal conflicts within the bolsonarist camp, while Ronaldo Caiado positions himself as an alternative to bolsonarism through strong ties to agribusiness and the São Paulo interior.

item.title: Vereadores do União Brasil são afastados por forjar candidaturas fantasmas de mulheres
item.description: Two União Brasil city councilors in Juazeiro (BA) were removed from office by the Federal Police for fabricating fake female candidacies in 2024 to violate gender quotas and misappropriate electoral funds. The women were recruited only to formally register as candidates without active campaign participation, and one was pressured to falsify documents at a notary to benefit a substitute councilor. The operation seized cash, electronic devices, and documents, with additional suspicions of vote-buying.

item.title: Flávio aposta em ataques e soma mais que o dobro do engajamento de Lula nas redes
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro leads social media engagement among 2026 presidential pre-candidates, averaging 183,000 interactions per post — more than double Lula’s (PT) 85,900 and triple Romeu Zema’s 59,700. While the electoral race remains tight in polls, digital engagement clearly favors the PL candidate. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Mendonça defende “grau de recatamento” no STF
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça urged judges to exercise greater restraint and prudence in public conduct to maintain judicial credibility. He emphasized impartiality, integrity, and responsibility, stating that office entails more duty than power. The remarks came amid pressure on the Court, including impeachment petitions against justices and revelations about travel tied to a former banker.

item.title: Depois de 'politicamente acabados', Bolsonaros voltam à cena com 'candidatura forte' de Flávio, diz FT
item.description: The Financial Times reported that the Bolsonaro family, deemed 'politically finished' at the end of 2023, is staging a comeback for the 2026 Brazilian elections, with Flávio Bolsonaro emerging as a highly competitive candidate. Described as the more moderate member of the family, Flávio contrasts with his father’s confrontational style and has publicly taken the Covid-19 vaccine, unlike Jair Bolsonaro. Despite high rejection rates, polls suggest he may be tied or ahead of Lula in voter intentions.

item.title: Confrontado sobre rachadinha, Flávio Bolsonaro recorre ao velho método de Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro announced his pre-candidacy for the presidency in December 2025, but was later confronted about a salary kickback scheme ('rachadinha') in the Rio de Janeiro State Legislative Assembly involving his former aide Fabrício Queiroz. In an interview, he claimed ignorance of the scheme, echoing Lula’s old defense strategy of denying knowledge and blaming subordinates. Despite preparation, the explanation was seen as weak, particularly given his lack of experience and ties to a chocolate shop investigated for money laundering linked to the kickbacks.

item.title: Vereadores do União Brasil são afastados por candidaturas falsas
item.description: The Federal Police launched an operation investigating an electoral fraud scheme in Juazeiro (BA), involving União Brasil councilors who violated gender quota rules by formally registering women as candidates without their effective participation in campaigns. Two councilors, Hitallo Marcelino and Anderson da Iluminação, were removed from office by the Electoral Justice, had their party activities suspended, and are barred from accessing the City Council or contacting public officials. The probe alleges misappropriation of electoral fund resources and coercion of a woman to formally acknowledge her candidacy as fictitious before a notary.

item.title: Guerra aumenta custos de projetos do governo para campanha de Lula
item.description: Rising oil, fuel, and food prices driven by the war are increasing the costs of government programs and threatening Lula's campaign, particularly the 'Gás do Povo' initiative, which aims to distribute subsidized gas canisters to 16 million households. The government has blamed businessmen for speculation but failed to acknowledge that the gas auction was organized by Petrobras, under government control, leading to the dismissal of a company official after pressure from the Civil Affairs and Energy Ministries. This leaves Lula disoriented, as he cannot control international prices or voter sentiment, making the campaign vulnerable to further cost escalation.

item.title: Caiado deixa governo aprovado por 84,7% dos goianos
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado's (PSD) government in Goiás is approved by 84.7% of voters, according to a Paraná Pesquisas survey released in April 2026, with 74.5% rating his administration as 'good' or 'excellent'. Caiado announced his pre-candidacy for President on March 30, 2026, stepping down from office. The study surveyed 1,310 people across 60 municipalities, with a margin of error of 2.8 percentage points and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: São toscas as versões de Flávio sobre esqueletos do seu armário
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro was accused of downplaying allegations of 'rachadinha' and ties to militias during an interview on the Inteligência Ltda. podcast, suggesting voters are naive to believe his explanations. The article criticizes his claims as unconvincing and politically motivated. These assertions are framed as part of a broader pattern of attempting to bury past scandals.

item.title: Eleições 2026: reajustes acima da inflação no serviço público estão vedados a partir desta terça (7)
item.description: Starting Tuesday (7), public agents are prohibited from granting salary adjustments above inflation in the public service during the 2026 election year, according to the Elections Law and TSE resolution. The measure aims to prevent the use of administrative structure to benefit candidacies, allowing only inflation compensation. The rule applies nationwide until the inauguration of elected officials, aiming to ensure equal opportunities and legitimacy in the electoral process.

item.title: A pesquisa Datafolha sobre o alto grau de endividamento da população
item.description: The Datafolha poll, launching today, includes questions on the high level of population indebtedness as a key factor in understanding Lula’s declining approval and the 2026 presidential race dynamics. The government views indebtedness as the main obstacle to boosting its popularity. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Daniel Vilela lidera disputa pelo governo de Goiás, diz pesquisa
item.description: Daniel Vilela (MDB), the current governor of Goiás, leads the 2026 gubernatorial race according to Paraná Pesquisas, with 43.4% voting intention in the scenario excluding Luis Cesar Bueno (PT) and 54% when excluding Marconi Perillo (PSDB). Marconi Perillo and Adriana Accorsi (PT) show the highest rejection rates at 37.3% and 21.6%, respectively. The survey interviewed 1,310 people across 60 municipalities from April 1–3, 2026, with a 2.8 percentage point margin of error and TSE registration GO-09885/2026.

item.title: Artigo: Quanto custa a democracia fluminense?
item.description: The article argues that direct election for governor of Rio de Janeiro is essential to democracy, even if costly, as it represents the political pact between citizen and ruler. It contends that Cláudio Castro's resignation to avoid judgment is a procedural maneuver that violates electoral law, and that Minister Cristiano Zanin's decision to uphold direct election is grounded in STF precedent and the Electoral Code. Replacing the will of 17 million voters with 70 parliamentarians is an attack on popular sovereignty and democratic integrity.

item.title: André do Prado prepara viagem aos EUA para debater vaga ao Senado
item.description: São Paulo Legislative Assembly President André do Prado (PL) is preparing a trip to the United States to meet with Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL) to discuss the PL’s second Senate seat nomination for São Paulo. The meeting comes as André gains internal party strength, backed by party president Valdemar Costa Neto and viewed favorably by Governor Tarcísio de Freitas. Although allies favor candidates like Mário Frias and Ricardo Mello Araújo, the final decision will require consensus between Jair and Eduardo Bolsonaro, with possible delays.

item.title: Cruzeiro estreia na Libertadores em ‘grupo da morte’ diante do Barcelona-EQU
item.description: Cruzeiro debuts in the 2026 Copa Libertadores against Barcelona-EQU in Group D, one of the tournament’s toughest groups alongside Universidad Católica and Boca Juniors. Despite a poor run in the Brazilian Série A — sitting second-to-last with seven points and coming off a 4-1 loss to São Paulo — coach Artur Jorge demands an immediate response in continental competition. Barcelona-EQU arrives on a seven-match unbeaten streak, featuring experienced striker Darío Benedetto, and is expected to field its strongest lineup.

item.title: A estratégia do PL para fazer com que presidente eleito pela Alerj possa assumiu o governo do Rio
item.description: The PL is asking the STF to allow the president of Alerj to assume the Rio de Janeiro government following the line of succession, citing the Amazonas precedent where Roberto Cidade assumed office after a vacancy. The election of Douglas Ruas as Alerj president was invalidated by a court decision, leaving the government under interim leadership of Ricardo Couto de Castro, president of TJ-RJ. The party argues for a 'symmetry norm' with other states, while the STF will also decide whether the interim mandate will be filled by direct election or a vote within Alerj.

item.title: O que falta até as eleições de 2026; veja as principais datas do TSE
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections are approaching with the TSE calendar already underway. Following the closure of the party transfer window, candidates are preparing for party conventions starting July 20, with official campaign propaganda beginning August 16 and election day set for October 4. Key dates include the candidacy registration deadline (August 15), the start of free radio and TV propaganda (August 28), and the availability of polling station lookup via e‑Título (September 1).

item.title: Quase 30% dos deputados mudam de legenda na janela partidária
item.description: Nearly 30% of federal deputies (138 out of 513) changed party affiliation during the 2026 party window, with the PL leading in new affiliations but Podemos achieving the largest net gain (+11 deputies). União Brasil suffered the largest losses (-29 departures, net -8), while the PT maintained a stable bench of 67 deputies. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) attracted 21 deputies to his presidential slate, yielding a net gain of +10 for his party.

item.title: Eleição na Câmara para escolher novo ministro do TCU pode ir parar no STF
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies is preparing voting booths for the election of a new minister at the Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) to fill the vacancy left by Aroldo Cedraz’s retirement. Expectations are that President Hugo Motta will convene the session tomorrow, following a leaders’ meeting scheduled for noon at the official residence. The article is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: RJ: Ao usar renúncia para burlar TSE, Castro comprometeu eleição indireta
item.description: Former Rio de Janeiro governor Claudio Castro resigned to avoid disqualification and ineligibility by the TSE, but the STF views this as an attempt to circumvent electoral law. This maneuver risks invalidating the indirect election meant to choose the state’s new governor, undermining the legitimacy of the process.

item.title: Bispo que dá apoio espiritual a Bolsonaro articula por Messias no STF: ‘Não sendo ele, será um pior’
item.description: Bishop Robson Rodovalho, a friend of Jair Bolsonaro and authorized by the STF to provide spiritual assistance to the former president, is rallying support for Lula’s nominee to the STF, Jorge Messias, who is also evangelical. He describes Messias as a 'genuine Christian' committed to faith, noting that despite being a petista, he does not support progressive agendas like drug decriminalization or abortion, making him the best left-wing option for evangelicals. Rodovalho criticizes Lula for not making intensive efforts to win over the evangelical vote and warned that if Messias is not chosen, Lula will nominate someone 'much worse'.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro consegue liminar para excluir postagens de quem o associa ao crime organizado
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for the Presidency of Brazil, obtained a preliminary injunction requiring Facebook to remove, within 48 hours, Instagram posts associating him with criminal organizations and the death of police officers. The ruling aims to curb the spread of content deemed defamatory by the legislator. Full access to the article is available only to subscribers.

item.title: Dança das cadeiras
item.description: The party window led to a congressional reorganization, with growth in the PL and PSD, maintaining right-wing dominance. Around 120 parliamentarians switched parties, consolidating Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL) presidential candidacy, while the PSD, led by Ronaldo Caiado, positions itself as a right-wing alternative, proposing amnesty for those involved in the January 8 attacks. The left retained the PT as its main party but lost PDT members, with the PSB growing — yet the rightward shift remains entrenched.

item.title: Reestruturação de carreiras do governo é avanço incremental, dizem analistas
item.description: Career restructuring in the Lula government is viewed by analysts as an incremental modernization, not a deep administrative transformation. Public management experts say the changes aim for efficiency and regulatory updates without overhauling existing structures.

item.title: Associações de juízes articulam obstáculo ao fim da aposentadoria compulsória como punição
item.description: Judges' associations are seeking to create a loophole in the PEC that abolishes compulsory retirement as punishment, proposing that removal from office depend on a final judicial decision. Rapporteur Eliziane Gama (PSB-MA) maintains the text aligned with Minister Flávio Dino's ruling, which requires the punishment to be ratified by the STF. Senators resist changes due to the election year and fear of public backlash.

item.title: Pacote anunciado pelo governo vai impedir a disparada dos preços dos combustíveis? Especialistas opinam
item.description: The Lula government announced a new package of measures to curb rising fuel prices, including subsidies for diesel, cooking gas (LPG), and aviation kerosene (QAV), credit for airlines, and strengthened oversight. The actions aim to mitigate the impact of surging oil prices due to the Middle East conflict, in an election year marked by inflation concerns.

item.title: Em 4 anos, força digital de Tarcísio superou a de Haddad, que precisará recuperar terreno nas eleições de 2026
item.description: Over the past four years, Tarcísio de Freitas surpassed Fernando Haddad in digital presence, growing from 2.9 million to 11.3 million followers, while Haddad remained at 7.6 million. This shift stems from Tarcísio’s aggressive content strategy, including videomakers and drone footage, contrasting with Haddad’s low-profile role as Finance Minister. Nonetheless, Haddad’s campaign asserts it will regain ground in the 2026 elections by prioritizing digital channels.

item.title: Space Liberdade: perfil no X que foi pivô de embate entre Eduardo e Nikolas é alvo frequente do ex-deputado
item.description: The 'Space Liberdade' profile on X, with around 450,000 followers and created in October 2023, became a focal point of a dispute between Eduardo Bolsonaro and Nikolas Ferreira after the Minas Gerais deputy shared a video from the page. Eduardo accused Keven Oliveira, identified as one of the profile's administrators, of 'preaching null votes,' while the account shares right-leaning news, religious messages, voting intention polls, and criticisms of Supreme Court ministers, alongside support for Bolsonarist agendas.

item.title: Com fim da janela partidária, PL amplia bancada na Alerj e fortalece apoio a Ruas
item.description: Following the party window, the PL expanded its bench in Alerj to 22 deputies, strengthening support for Douglas Ruas in the race for the Assembly presidency and interim Rio governorship. The party now totals 33 deputies with União Brasil and PP, just three shy of the majority needed in an indirect election. The PSD, led by Eduardo Paes, rose from six to ten deputies and is building an alliance with PT, PCdoB, PSB, PDT and MDB to reach at least 20 votes, awaiting judicial rulings that could level the playing field.

item.title: Desenho de candidaturas à Presidência indica primeira disputa sem mulheres desde 2002
item.description: The current outline of presidential candidacies for 2026 includes no women, which, if confirmed, would mark the first time since 2002 that the race for the Planalto features only men. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) are the leading figures so far. Experts say the absence of female candidates reflects structural party barriers that hinder women’s representation in executive offices.

item.title: Aneel vota nesta terça processo que pode cassar contrato da Enel em SP
item.description: Aneel is set to vote on Tuesday (April 7) on a process that could lead to the cancellation of Enel’s contract in São Paulo, following blackouts in 2023 and 2024 and service failures. The administrative procedure, previously suspended by a court injunction, has been reinstated after a judicial decision and may result in the concession’s forfeiture, valid until 2028, with the final decision resting with the federal government.

item.title: Como Nikolas foi de bolsonarista raiz a protagonista de racha na direita
item.description: Nikolas Ferreira, once a key strategist of Bolsonarism and Brazil's most-voted federal deputy in 2022, has become the target of public criticism from Eduardo Bolsonaro over alleged endorsements of Bolsonarism’s enemies, exposing an internal rift in the right-wing movement. The conflict reveals a struggle for leadership and influence within Bolsonarism, with Nikolas allegedly orchestrating a boycott of Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential bid.

item.title: Para garantir prorrogação, CPI do Crime pode se distanciar do Master, diz relator
item.description: The Organized Crime CPI seeks to extend its work by 60 days but plans to distance itself from investigations into Banco Master to avoid resistance from Senate President Davi Alcolumbre during an election year. Rapporteur Alessandro Vieira states that frauds linked to Daniel Vorcaro fall within the committee’s scope, but the focus will now shift to militias and criminal factions, while also advocating for a separate CPI to investigate Master.

item.title: Acordo entre Goiás e EUA sobre minerais vira alvo de ação na PGR
item.description: Deputy Dandara Tonantzin (PT-MG) has asked the PGR to investigate the constitutionality of a memorandum of understanding between the state of Goiás and the United States regarding critical minerals and rare earths, arguing that the agreement oversteps state authority and invades federal jurisdiction, as mineral resources belong to the Union. Governor Ronaldo Caiado signed the agreement on March 18 with U.S. Charge d'Affaires Gabriel Escobar in São Paulo, aiming to prioritize rare earth exploration in Goiás and secure funding for studies. The deputy alleges possible administrative impropriety, usurpation of public office, and other illegalities in the act.

item.title: Diretas são única saída legal para a sucessão no Rio
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) will rule tomorrow on the injunction that suspended the indirect election for Rio de Janeiro's interim governor following Claudio Castro's (PL) resignation. The article argues that Castro's resignation was a maneuver to avoid impeachment and retain political control, insisting that succession must occur through a direct election as mandated by law. Amid Rio's political crisis, the Court must uphold constitutional order and prevent electoral fraud disguised as institutional transition.

item.title: O voto é a voz do Rio
item.description: Former Governor Claudio Castro resigned on the eve of his TSE cassation over serious electoral crimes, seeking to evade Article 224 of the Electoral Code and replace the popular vote with a legislative appointment by Alerj, in an alleged constitutional fraud. The article condemns this maneuver as an affront to democracy and the rule of law.

item.title: Líderes da Câmara tentam acordo para votar indicação ao TCU nesta semana
item.description: Chamber leaders set the date for the TCU minister election, expected this Wednesday, following internal agreements. The vote is seen as a test of strength for Chamber President Hugo Motta, who aims to secure Odair Cunha’s (PT-MG) victory to fulfill a 2024 deal with the PT, despite internal resistance. The secret ballot includes candidates such as Hugo Leal, Elmar Nascimento, Hélio Lopes, Danilo Forte, Adriana Ventura, and Gilson Daniel, filling the vacancy left by Aroldo Cedraz.

item.title: Caiado, Tebet, Moro, Pacheco: veja políticos que trocaram de partido para disputar a eleição
item.description: Following the closure of the party switching window in April, several prominent politicians changed parties ahead of the 2026 elections. Ronaldo Caiado left União Brasil for the PSD to run for president; Sergio Moro moved to the PL to pursue the governorship of Paraná; Simone Tebet exited the MDB after 30 years to join the PSB and run for Senate in São Paulo; and Rodrigo Pacheco shifted from PSD to PSB in Minas Gerais, with federal government backing, eyeing a gubernatorial bid.
